the plan reviewer is given the steering body with its version, as that package defines both, and quotes a steering finding's directive against that body

tasks.title: Add the two phase names and give every tier their model and effort
steps: Add the tier and per-phase behaviours to internal/agentrun/models_test.go, extending TestResolvePlan_ATierChoosesAModelPerPhase and TestParsePhaseChoice, and confirm they fail

In internal/agentrun/models.go add PhasePlanReview = "plan_review" and PhasePlanRevision = "plan_revision" beside the PRD review's constants, and put both into Phases after PhaseTasks so the ordered list reads in the order a package is built

In tierTable give each of the three tiers an explicit entry for both phases equal to that tier's requirements entry: sonnet-5-5 at medium for SIMPLE, sonnet-5-5 at high for STANDARD and opus-5-5 at high for ADVANCED — ADVANCED's base is xhigh, so leaving them to base would not give the effort the table asks for
Confirm a per-phase model choice naming either phase parses and applies to that phase alone, the parser reading the name from Phases
Document the two phase names in docs/configuration.md among those a per-phase model choice accepts, and in the phase table of docs/cli.md

tasks.title: Compute the grounding facts and add the plan review phase with its rubrics
steps: Add the grounding behaviours to a new specgen/grounding_test.go, the prompt behaviours to specgen/prompts_test.go and the reviewer's checks to a new specgen/plan_review_tool_test.go, and confirm they fail

Add specgen/grounding.go: for every path in every task's touches, resolve it with workspace.Resolve and call os.Stat, reporting it as existing when the stat succeeds whether it is a file or a directory, and as not existing when the resolve or the stat fails — so a path outside the repository root is not existing; keep one entry per distinct path in task order and then touches order

Add specgen/plan_review_tool.go with the terminating tool of the plan review: the submission schema of the PRD review's plus a rubric enum of zero_decision, grounding and steering, with the description of each, and the same 30-finding cap

Check every finding over the whole submission and report every offender in one error, as the PRD review's tool does: an empty severity, section, flaw, evidence or remedy, naming the fields; a rubric or a severity outside its set; and more than 30 findings, naming the count and the cap

Check a finding's section against the plan under review: accept a test id, a criterion id or an execution path id of this plan, or a task of it named by its number, and refuse anything else naming the position, the section and the kinds of place a section may name

Check a grounding finding that says a path does not exist: the path it names must be one the grounding facts list, and a finding naming any other path is refused, naming the position and the path; a finding of another rubric is not checked this way

Check a steering finding as the PRD review's tool does: its evidence must quote a passage appearing in the steering body under sameEvidence's normalisation, and its severity must not be minor, each refusal naming the position and what is wrong

Add specgen/templates/plan_review_system.md with both rubrics in full — the five questions of the Zero-Decision Rule and the four of grounding, as the package's requirements give them — the three severities with their meaning for a plan, the rule that every finding names its rubric and its place by id, and the steering rubric

Add specgen/templates/plan_review_user.md and the prompt builders in specgen/prompts.go: the PRD as it stands, the rendered plan, the grounding facts, the codebase notes introduced as the author's claims to check, and the earlier rounds' findings; carry no part of the input body and no part of the context block

Render the plan for both phases from the artifacts held in memory, through (*RequirementsV2Json).Render, (*TestSpecV2Json).Render and (*TasksV2Json).Render in that order under their own headings, with no scope and no budget, so each section is byte-identical to the package's own render of that artifact

Add specgen/templates/plan_revision_user.md and its builder with the PRD, the plan, this round's findings, the grounding facts, the codebase notes and the same project context, and no part of the input

Add a Review method for the plan to the reviewer interface in specgen/phases.go and implement it on agentAuthor through reviewPhase, so the phase gets the read-only file tools, the code-search index, the run context block and the token ceiling every review phase gets

tasks.title: Add the plan revision phase and the checks on what it may change
steps: Add the revision's behaviours to a new specgen/plan_revision_tool_test.go, and confirm they fail

Add specgen/plan_revision_tool.go with the terminating tool of the plan revision: the three plan artifacts submitted whole, and the answers in the shape the PRD review's revision tool takes, so the four dispositions and their checks are the same code path

Refuse a submission that changes the PRD body, the spec id or spec name in any artifact, the state of a task, or the actors of the execution paths, with one error naming each kind of change and where; compare actors by name ignoring case so reordering the paths or a path's steps is no change

Refuse a submission whose plan does not pass afspec.ValidateGenerationStepComplete(afspec.StepTasks, partial), with one error naming every rule it broke, each with the artifact and the entity it is about, so the phase asks again until it passes or runs out of turns or budget

Refuse a declined answer to a finding whose rubric is steering, with one error naming the id and its rubric and saying such a finding is fixed, contested or escalated; leave a finding of either other rubric free to be declined with a reason

Add specgen/templates/plan_revision_system.md: what the reviser may change and what it may not, that it submits all three artifacts whole, that the revised plan must pass the format's own rules, and the four dispositions with what each requires as the PRD revision's prompt gives them
Add a Revise method for the plan to the reviewer interface in specgen/phases.go and implement it on agentAuthor through reviewPhase, with the plan revision phase name

tasks.title: Wire the stage into the pipeline behind its flag, with the gate before the first round
steps: Add the ordering, the flag-independence, the dry-run, the gate and the last-complete-plan behaviours to specgen/pipeline_test.go, and confirm they fail

Add AdversarialPlan to specgen.Options beside Adversarial, and register --adversarial-plan in cmd/spec/main.go with the sentence that a fresh agent looks for the flaws in every plan the run generates and another revises it, and pass it through specOptions

In buildPackage in specgen/pipeline.go, after the last generation step and before the architecture phase, validate the plan with afspec.ValidateGenerationStepComplete(afspec.StepTasks, partial) when the flag is on

When that validation fails, raise one high warning of a new code naming the scope and the number of errors, run no round, and fall through to the write and the verdict so the run fails on the same errors with the same exit code as a run without the flag

When it passes, compute the grounding facts once for the package and run the rounds, then set spec.Requirements, spec.TestSpec and spec.Tasks from the plan the rounds returned, so the architecture phase and the write both get the last complete plan
Confirm the two review flags stay independent: each is read on its own, each takes its own rounds, and a run with neither runs exactly the phases it runs today
Confirm a dry run bills the two phases and carries the record while writing nothing, the validation and the verdict being taken over the plan held in memory
Describe the plan review in docs/architecture.md as a stage of the pipeline between the tasks phase and the architecture phase, and add --adversarial-plan and the skipped warning to docs/cli.md

tasks.title: Run the plan rounds on the PRD review's rules, and survive a phase that fails
steps: Add the round-loop, failure, budget, progress and ceiling behaviours to specgen/rounds_test.go, specgen/phases_test.go and specgen/pipeline_test.go, and confirm they fail

Add the plan's round loop to specgen/rounds.go beside runRounds, sharing its structure: a round is one review and, when the review raised anything, one revision; each round after the first is handed the earlier findings with their answers; and the ids are of the same form

Apply the triage, the repeat rules and the two-clean-round convergence of the PRD review unchanged, so the stop reason is converged, rounds_exhausted or incomplete and never another value, and the record carries the same per-round and per-finding fields and the same six totals

When a plan review or revision ends without a result, stop the rounds, hand back the last complete plan, and raise one high warning of a new code naming the scope, the round, plan_review or plan_revision, and why it failed
Mark every finding of a round whose revision did not finish unanswered, leaving the earlier rounds' answers as they were
Check the total budget before each plan review and each plan revision, stopping the rounds the same way and naming what the run has spent of what ceiling in the warning
Let neither failure change whether the run fails or its exit code, and keep a cancelled context failing the run as aborted at the phase it stopped, as the PRD rounds do
Report each phase on the progress stream with its scope and the round out of the limit, and report what each review raised counted by severity
Give each plan phase the whole of every per-phase budget, turn, timeout and token ceiling through reviewPhase, as a PRD review phase gets them
Add the two warning codes to envelope/warn.go and internal/cli/warn.go with their stage, and document both in docs/cli.md

tasks.title: Make the rounds flag serve both reviews and price the stage in the preflight
steps: Add the flag-grammar cases to cmd/spec/main_test.go and the preflight cases to specgen/pipeline_test.go, and confirm they fail

In PreCheck in cmd/spec/main.go refuse the rounds flag when neither --adversarial nor --adversarial-plan is given, with a message naming its value and both flags, and keep the 1-to-5 range check as it is
Confirm the rounds flag is read as the limit for each review separately, so with both reviews on and a limit of 3 a package may run up to twelve review and revision phases

In RunPreflight in specgen/pipeline.go count two more phases per allowed round per package still to be written when the plan review is on, beside the two the PRD review already adds, as an upper bound
In phaseModels name plan_review and plan_revision when the plan review is on and omit them when it is off, as it already does for the PRD review's two phases
Update docs/cli.md for the new meaning of --adversarial-rounds, the preflight's phase count with each review, and the usage error

steps: Add the split behaviours to specgen/split_run_test.go, and confirm they fail
Keep the plan rounds inside each scope's own package build in specgen/pipeline.go, not in the split coordinator where the PRD rounds run, so the next scope's PRD phase is not made to wait for them
Confirm the next scope's PRD and requirements phases start while a scope's plan rounds are still running, within the run's parallelism limit

Note in docs/architecture.md where a scope's plan rounds run, beside the note on where its PRD rounds run

Add the plan review's clause to the summary sentence in specgen/pipeline.go beside the PRD review's, naming the rounds run, the findings raised and the number fixed, counted over every package of the run, and leaving it out when no plan was reviewed
Keep the plan review's record out of nothing the summary view keeps: carry it under --detail summary without its rounds, as the PRD review's record is carried

Give the plan reviewer the steering body with its version, from the same run environment value the other phases read, so the prompt carries the directives and the instruction to check the plan against them

Document the plan review record and the new summary clause in docs/cli.md, and the two rubrics and what a steering finding needs

tasks.title: Verify the four paths end to end and record the stage in an ADR
steps: Add the four end-to-end cases to cmd/spec/main_test.go, beside TestAdversarial_GeneratesThePackageFromTheRevisedPRD and TestPreflight_ReportsTheChecklistAndWritesNothing, each against a real temporary repository and the scripted model, and confirm they pass

Trace 18-PATH-1 from the generated plan through the in-memory validation, the grounding facts, the review and the revision to the corrected touches in the written tasks.json, and confirm each step calls the next with no stub left
Trace 18-PATH-2 from the invalid plan through the gate to the warning and the unchanged failure, and confirm no plan phase was billed
Trace 18-PATH-3 from the split coordinator through each scope's own package build to three plan review records, and confirm the next scope's PRD phase overlapped the previous scope's rounds
Trace 18-PATH-4 from the preflight flags to the phase count and the two phase models, and confirm no model call was made

For every criterion with a contract, confirm a caller in production code consumes the producer's result and not only a test: the pipeline consumes the in-memory validation and the grounding facts, the review tool consumes the plan and the facts, the round loop consumes the reviewer's findings and the reviser's plan, the write consumes the last complete plan, and the summary consumes the record
Grep specgen/, envelope/, internal/agentrun/ and cmd/spec/ for TODO and panic("not implemented") and remove any that remain
Confirm the plan review's prompts carry no part of the run's input: grep the recorded prompts of an end-to-end run for the input body and the context block

Write the ADR as docs/adr/NN-review-the-plan-adversarially.md, NN being the next free number by the rule in CLAUDE.md, recording the stage's own flag and why it is not part of --adversarial, the two rubrics, the grounding facts as computed rather than judged, that an invalid plan is not reviewed, that the reviser may change the three artifacts and not the actors, and the two new phase names with their tier entries
Run make doc and then make check
